transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-08-30 14:00 PDT
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Greenline Head of Platform), Devon (SRE), Anita (ML Eng)

00:00 Jordan: okay hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Friday, um quick agenda — staging handoff, kv/prefix cache results, and then plan a perf run. If we run short on any of the SSO bits we can follow up next week.
00:18 Marta: sounds good, should be about 45 mins, we've got Devon and Anita on to confirm network and sample prompts
00:25 Priya: hi hi — Priya from Redwood, I'll be driving the kv cache checks and the tuning notes.
00:30 Devon: morning, Devon here, SRE, I'll talk peering and firewall stuff.
00:34 Anita: Anita — ML eng, i've got the prompt set and a sample traffic export ready, just need to confirm format.
00:42 Jordan: perfect. quick sync on status: we handed over the initial staging cluster yesterday, credentials were posted to the secure vault, correct? Marta?
00:50 Marta: yep repo and temp creds are in but dev team flagged missing KMS access and SSO mapping looked off. We haven't yet rotated keys.
01:02 Jordan: ok good call — rotation and KMS are gating for you to run real traffic. Priya, can we do something temporary like scoped API key + ephemeral creds so they can kick off a small benchmark?
01:12 Priya: yes, we can enable ephemeral token flow and a scoped key for the perf window. It's not ideal long term but fine for the initial run. We'll also instrument prefix-hit metrics so we can see cache warmup.
01:23 Devon: on our side we'd prefer the VPC peering before hitting infra, at a minimum firewall allow-lists. Can the ephemeral token bypass be limited to Redwood IPs?
01:33 Priya: yes we can restrict by IP CIDR and also accept a customer-signed cert on the gateway. We'll include guidance in the runbook.
01:42 Anita: about the prompt set — do you need raw user utterances or de-identified examples? Privacy's the concern.
01:49 Jordan: sanitized is fine, ideally redact pii but keep length distribution and common system prompts, so perf represents real usage.
01:58 Anita: got it, i'll produce that and upload. question — when you say prefix cache, does that mean the kv cache stores token prefixes across sessions or only per request?
02:09 Priya: good question. Redwood's cache keeps recent KV state for active sessions and supports prefix caching for common prompts — it's not a full convo store unless you opt-in to long-lived KV. For this POC we plan short TTL so cache warms within the test window. Also note the term in our docs might appear as 'KV cache' or 'prefix cache' — doc OCR sometimes shows 'K V cache' which is confusing.
02:29 Marta: ha yeah we've seen that in the docs. Another ask from security — we need the audit log sample (format and retention). Do you have a quick example?
02:38 Jordan: yes i'll send the audit log snippet and retention policy. SOC2 stuff is in the trust center link, i'll include a short write-up.
02:45 Devon: note on peering — our networking team needs the target subnets and a triage window. We have a maint slot on Thursday 9/3. Is that viable?
02:54 Priya: that works, we can schedule traffic to start after the peering is established; we'll coordinate for minimal blast radius.
03:03 Jordan: now onto perf tradeoffs — Marta earlier said SLA target is 300–400ms p99 for short completion tasks, is that still the goal?
03:12 Marta: yes for the trimmed prompts, but for longer multi-turn it's okay to be higher. The critical product flows (search rerank + short answer) should be tight.
03:20 Priya: okay, so we'll do two bench passes: 1) small prompts (<=192 tokens) to exercise prefix cache and lower latency paths; 2) long prompts to measure kv cold/warm behavior. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
03:36 Anita: about cost — we want a sense of token cost at scale; can you give a quick example for batch size / quantization options?
03:44 Jordan: sure — rough callouts: hosted burst mode is cheaper for light intermittent traffic, while reserved capacity (Dedicated) becomes cost efficient at steady high throughput. Quantization helps per-token cost but might add latency for certain kernels; Priya can share quant profiles we've used.
03:58 Priya: yes — for M6-style weights we recommend 4-bit quant for inference; we've observed ~1.6x cost reduction but watch for slight quality diffs on very sensitive prompts. We'll attach a quantization note in the runbook.
04:12 Devon: any blockers from Redwood infra side for enabling KMS integration? Customer needs BYOK path.
04:18 Priya: we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS/HSM integrations; the private deployment has a different flow but for this POC we can demo KMS-encrypted storage for model artifacts and key wrapping. We'll include steps in the KMS section.
04:31 Anita: great. one more thing — can you surface a KV cache hit rate during the perf run? We want to correlate hit-rate with latency changes.
04:38 Priya: yes we'll surface prefix-hit-rate, per-model kv-hit, and sample token timings. We'll also export raw traces you can ingest.
04:45 Jordan: ok next, on security questionnaire that Marta mentioned — are there any parts that usually take extra time? Marta?
04:51 Marta: the encryption-at-rest section and third-party subprocessors list tend to require legal signoff, but the SOC2 summary helps. We'll need Redwood's DPA in parallel.
04:59 Jordan: we'll include DPA draft and subprocessors list with the SOC2 link.
05:05 Devon: timeline recap — peering window 9/3, perf run target 9/7, deliverables due by early next week. Does Redwood have any objections?
05:14 Priya: that's fine. We'll prepare the runbook and a minimal helm values file so your infra team can apply a test namespace.
05:22 Anita: about metrics — will the run include token-level cost?
05:27 Priya: yes, we'll emit per-request token counts and cost estimate using the model's tokenization baseline; it's approximate but useful for planning.
05:36 Jordan: alright let's call out action owners — Priya you'll share runbook + helm values; Jordan sends security links; Anita uploads sanitized traffic; Devon coordinates peering. We'll reconvene after the perf run to interpret results.
05:51 Marta: sounds good. any other items?
05:55 Devon: small ask — can Redwood provide a fallback path if peering slips, e.g., IP-restricted temporary access?
06:02 Priya: yes that's the plan — ephemeral token + IP allowlist as a fallback. We'll include rollback steps in the runbook.
06:10 Jordan: great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and action items in email.
06:15 Marta: thanks all, speak soon.

Post-call notes (moderate transcription errors expected):
- There was a brief crosstalk when discussing KMS vs BYOK, transcript may show 'K M S BY OK' in a few spots.
- Reference to 'M6' was shorthand for the customer's chosen model family, might be mis-transcribed as 'M six'.

References shared in-chat: staging runbook link, kv prefix dashboard, SOC2 summary, traffic upload instructions.

End of transcript.
